title: Ordinary etale compact-support scalar compatibility with projection and composition
statement:
Let $A\to A'$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between Noetherian schemes, each admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Choose a compactification $f=pj$, with $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ open and $p:\overline X\to Y$ proper [def-asd-compactifiable]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-ring module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with $Q_T=(-)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Use the canonical K-flat tensor/pullback identifications [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the usual tensor unit $Q_T(A_T[0])\cong A'_T[0]$ induced by multiplication.

Put $F_{f,R}=Rf_{!,R}=Rp_{*,R}j_{!,R}$ for $R=A,A'$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Define $q_f:Q_YF_{f,A}\to F_{f,A'}Q_X$ by the proper scalar map of [lem-asd-proper-finite-coefficient-extension] evaluated at $j_{!,A}(-)$, followed by $Rp_{*,A'}$ of the open scalar tensor map $Q_{\overline X}j_{!,A}\cong j_{!,A'}Q_X$. The latter is the canonical balancing map: on the open it is scalar tensor, and off the open it is the zero-module map; its inverse is the open-adjunction transpose of the scalar extension of the open unit. Let $P_{f,R;K,M}:K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F_{f,R}M\to F_{f,R}(f^*K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)$ be the proper-counit/open-tensor projection transformation [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection, lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor].

Then $q_f$ is a natural isomorphism on the entire derived category. For every $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ the specified morphisms satisfy
$$q_{f,f^*K\otimes M}\circ Q_Y(P_{f,A;K,M})=P_{f,A';Q_YK,Q_XM}\circ(1\otimes q_{f,M}),$$
after the canonical scalar tensor and scalar/pullback identifications of source and target. For composable compactifiable separated finite-type morphisms $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow g Z$ between Noetherian schemes, use the proper/open triangle-normalized compact-support composition $\alpha_R:F_{g,R}F_{f,R}\cong F_{gf,R}$ [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. If $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $Q_XM\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A')$, then
$$q_{gf,M}\circ Q_Z(\alpha_{A,M})=\alpha_{A',Q_XM}\circ F_{g,A'}(q_{f,M})\circ q_{g,F_{f,A}M}.$$
For an open immersion $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$, put $X_V=f^{-1}(V)$, $f_V:X_V\to V$, $v_X:X_V\hookrightarrow X$, and give $f_V$ the restricted compactification $X_V\hookrightarrow p^{-1}(V)\to V$. Then, for every $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the specified maps satisfy $$C_{f,v,A'}(Q_XM)\circ v^*(q_{f,M})=q_{f_V,v_X^*M}\circ Q_V(C_{f,v,A}(M)),$$ where $C_{f,v,R}:v^*F_{f,R}\cong F_{f_V,R}v_X^*$ is the compact-support exchange of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], and the source $v^*Q_YF_{f,A}M$ is identified with $Q_Vv^*F_{f,A}M$ and $v_X^*Q_XM$ with $Q_{X_V}v_X^*M$ by the canonical scalar/pullback identifications. These comparisons respect proper refinements of compactifications on these bounded-below inputs and the canonical coefficient-unit identification. No flatness or finite projective dimension of $A'$ over $A$, smoothness of $f$, orientation, or exceptional-pullback coefficient comparison is assumed.

proof.text: Write $U_T$ for restriction of scalars and $\lambda_u:u_{A'}^*Q_T\cong Q_Wu_A^*$ for $u:W\to T$. The cited derived tensor/pullback result applies both to $u$ and to the identity topos with ring map $A_T\to A'_T$: it supplies K-flat representatives with flat terms and the scalar tensor comparison $\mu:Q(H\otimes_A^L K)\cong QH\otimes_{A'}^L QK$. These canonical comparisons are compatible with composition, symmetry and the unit. Here is the representative check needed below. The inverse of $\mu$ sends $(x\otimes a')\otimes(y\otimes b')$ to $(x\otimes y)\otimes a'b'$. Both iterated scalar/pullback comparisons send a pulled-back generator $x\otimes a'$ to the same pulled-back $x\otimes a'$. Associativity is $(a'b')c'=a'(b'c')$; symmetry has the same sign $(-1)^{|x||y|}$ on both paths, and the unit is $a\otimes b'\mapsto\varphi(a)b'$. The sheaf inverse-image composition identifications are module-linear. These identities on total K-flat tensor complexes descend by the cited tensor-localization statement; no flatness of $A'$ over $A$ is involved.

proof.text: For an open $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, extension by zero carries K-flat complexes with flat terms to K-flat complexes with flat terms. Indeed the sheaf tensor identity, applied in each bidegree and summed along total degrees, gives $(j_!P)\otimes_A H\cong j_!(P\otimes_A j^*H)$. Extension by zero commutes with these sums by its cited adjunction on sheaves: $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!(\bigoplus P_i),H)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(P_i,j^*H)=\operatorname{Hom}(\bigoplus j_!P_i,H)$, naturally in $H$. If $H$ is acyclic, exactness of $j^*$ makes $j^*H$ acyclic, K-flatness of $P$ makes the inner tensor acyclic, and exactness of $j_!$ makes the result acyclic. For a single flat term $P^i$, apply the same identity to a short exact sequence $H$; this proves flatness of $j_!P^i$. This is just the defining acyclicity and exactness tests, not a finite Tor-amplitude assertion.

proof.text: For the open normalization there is a shorter adjunction argument, implemented in compactScalarOpen_normalization. Transport the exact open adjunctions to left-derived pullback using leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory. The published ExceptionalCoefficients.openIso is the conjugate under the composite open/scalar adjunctions. Apply iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_symm: its inverse is the open mate of the inverse scalar-restriction mate. The proved private scalarPullback_eq of lem-sfb-etale-proetale-scalar-mate identifies this inner mate with scalarPullbackIso.inv. Apply unit_mateEquiv_symm and transport back to exact pullback. Naturality of the exact-pullback comparison and cancellation of its inverse and forward components identify the transpose with properOpenCoefficientOpenInverse. Injectivity of the open adjunction Hom equivalence proves the required equality on every unbounded input, without a fresh K-flat calculation.

proof.text:
On the fixed compactification put $\chi_p=\beta_p$ of [lem-asd-proper-finite-coefficient-extension]. It is an isomorphism on every derived input, normalized as the transpose of $Q(\varepsilon_{p,A})\lambda_p$. Step 3 gives an isomorphism $\beta_j$. Hence
$$q_f=Rp_{*,A'}(\beta_j)\circ\chi_p(j_{!,A}(-))$$
is a natural isomorphism on the entire category, with exactly the specified normalization. The ambient compactification is Noetherian because its proper map to $Y$ is finite type and $Y$ is Noetherian. Open subschemes used below are Noetherian as well, by the cited open-subscheme result. Thus the geometric hypotheses of the proper coefficient comparison hold here and on every restricted compactification. Naturality is implemented separately as compactScalarMap_naturality: use scalarMate.naturality on the open-extension image of a morphism, then openIso.hom.naturality, and combine the latter maps using proper direct-image functoriality.

Apply the ringed exchange/tensor coherence theorem to the square whose vertical arrows are $p$ with $A$- and $A'$-coefficients and whose horizontal arrows are identity topoi with structural ring maps $A\to A'$. Its exchange is $\chi_p$, since both are the transpose of $Q(\varepsilon_{p,A})\lambda_p$. The theorem gives compatibility of scalar extension with the proper projection map on arbitrary $K,E$. It states the projection with $Rp_*E$ first; apply the two tensor symmetries from [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] and Step 1 to obtain, in the order used here,
$$\chi_{p,p^*K\otimes E}\,Q(P_{p,A;K,E})=P_{p,A';QK,QE}(1\otimes\chi_{p,E}).$$
The target uses $Q(p^*K\otimes E)\cong p^*QK\otimes QE$. No cartesianness of the ringed-topos square, boundedness, or Tor-amplitude hypothesis is needed by that theorem.

proof.text:
Let $O_{j,H,M}:H\otimes_A^Lj_!M\cong j_!(j^*H\otimes_A^LM)$ be the open tensor map, obtained from the map in [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor] by symmetry. For K-flat $H$ and $M$ with flat terms, Steps 1--3 compute its scalar extension and both open scalar maps by actual total tensor complexes. In each bidegree the two routes send a section $(h\otimes m)\otimes a'$ supported on $U$ to $(j^*h\otimes m)\otimes a'$; on the zero summand both maps are zero. The symmetries introduce the same Koszul signs. Consequently, after sheafification, totalization and localization, these routes are equal:
$$\beta_{j,j^*H\otimes M}\,Q(O_{j,H,M})=O_{j,QH,QM}(1\otimes\beta_{j,M}).$$
The canonical scalar tensor and pullback maps in this equation are those of Step 1. The cited K-flat localization statement makes the calculation natural on the whole pair of derived categories.

proof.text:
By the definition of the compactified projection transformation,
$$P_{f,R;K,M}=Rp_{*,R}(O_{j,p^*K,M})\circ P_{p,R;K,j_!M}.$$
Substitute this formula and Step 4's formula for $q_f$ into the desired projection equation. Naturality of $\chi_p$ moves $Q(O_{j,p^*K,M})$ through $\chi_p$. Step 5 changes the adjacent proper projection/scalar composite to $P_{p,A'}(1\otimes\chi_p)$. Step 6 changes the adjacent open tensor/scalar composite to $O_{j,A'}(1\otimes\beta_j)$. Combining the last two factors gives $1\otimes q_f$ by Step 4. The result is exactly $P_{f,A';QK,QM}(1\otimes q_f)$; thus the claimed equation holds for every $K,M$. Only substitution and naturality remain after Steps 5--6.

proof.text:
There are two elementary composition identities for the constituent scalar maps. For composable proper maps $r,s$, identify $R(sr)_*$ with $Rs_*Rr_*$ by the cited canonical direct-image composition. Its K-injective normalization is the right-adjoint comparison: on resolved morphisms the canonical derived adjunction of [def-kun-projection-formula-map] is the composite termwise Hom bijection, using the module-linear inverse-image composition from Step 1. Mate pasting applied to the pullback/scalar squares of Step 1 gives
$$\chi_{sr}=Rs_{*,A'}(\chi_r)\circ\chi_s(Rr_{*,A}(-)).$$
Indeed the composite counit is $\varepsilon_r\circ r^*(\varepsilon_s)$, so both transposes are $Q(\varepsilon_r)\,Qr^*(\varepsilon_s)$ after the pullback identifications. For composable opens $a,b$, use the canonical extension composition. The inverses of $\beta_{ba}$ and $b_{!,A'}\beta_a\circ\beta_b(a_{!,A}(-))$ have identical transposes under $(ba)_!\dashv(ba)^*$: both are scalar extension of the composite open unit. Equivalently they are the identity on the same unique open summand. This proves scalar compatibility with direct-image composition and open-extension composition, on unbounded inputs.

proof.text:
Consider a proper refinement $u:T_1\to T_2$ of compactifications, with $uj_1=j_2$, and put $p_1=p_2u$. For $M$ and $Q_XM$ bounded below, apply [lem-sf-proper-open-coefficient-refinement] to exactly these maps and coefficient rings. Its displayed equality says
$$Ru_{*,A'}(\beta_{j_1})\,\chi_u\,Q(\alpha_{u,A})=\alpha_{u,A'}\,\beta_{j_2}.$$
Its $\chi_u$ and $\beta_{j_a}$ have precisely the counit and open-unit normalizations of Steps 3--4. Apply $Rp_{2,*,A'}$ to this equality and use Step 8 for $p_2u$. The result is the square comparing $q_f$ for the two compactifications and their proper-refinement maps. The cited compact-support comparison theorem identifies these with the specified refinement comparisons and gives their cocycle identity. It follows by composing these squares and inverting refinement isomorphisms that scalar compatibility also holds for comparisons through common refinements. This use is confined to the stated bounded-below pair of inputs.

proof.text:
Use the normalized tower in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]: $Y\xrightarrow{i}\overline Y\xrightarrow{s}Z$, $X\xrightarrow{a}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}\overline Y$, and $V=p^{-1}(Y)$ with $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $r:V\to Y$, $j:X\hookrightarrow V$, $bj=a$. Thus $F_f=Rr_*j_!$, $F_g=Rs_*i_!$ and $F_{gf}=R(sp)_*(bj)_!$. The composition comparison is $Rs_*\Gamma$, followed by proper and open composition, where $\Gamma:i_!Rr_*\cong Rp_*b_!$. For $E=j_{!,A}M$, exactness of open extension gives $E\in D^+$, and Step 3 identifies $Q_VE$ with $j_{!,A'}Q_XM\in D^+$. The coefficient clause of [lem-sp-proper-open-coefficient-mate] therefore applies to the cartesian proper/open square and gives
$$Rp_{*,A'}\beta_b\,\chi_p\,Q\Gamma_A=\Gamma_{A'}\,i_{!,A'}\chi_r\,\beta_i.$$
Paste this square with the scalar squares for $j_!$ and $Rs_*$ and Step 8's two composition identities. The left boundary is $q_{gf,M}Q_Z(\alpha_{A,M})$, and the right boundary is $\alpha_{A',Q_XM}F_{g,A'}(q_{f,M})q_{g,F_{f,A}M}$, as required. Step 9 permits all other compactification choices: for $gf$ and $f$ it is applied to $M$, and for $g$ to $F_{f,A}M$. The latter input satisfies the hypotheses of Step 9: $j_{!,A}M\in D^+$ by exactness of open extension, a bounded-below complex has a bounded-below injective, hence K-injective, resolution, so $F_{f,A}M=Rr_{*,A}j_{!,A}M\in D^+$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; and by Step 4, $Q_YF_{f,A}M\cong F_{f,A'}Q_XM$, which lies in $D^+$ by the same argument applied to $Q_XM\in D^+$. All ambient schemes in this tower are Noetherian by the finite-type and open-subscheme facts used in Step 4.

proof.text:
For the proper part of the open restriction square write $w:p^{-1}(V)\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $p_V:p^{-1}(V)\to V$, and $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$. Let $B_R:v_R^*Rp_{*,R}\to Rp_{V,*,R}w_R^*$ be the exchange of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. For every unbounded $E$ its coefficient square is
$$Rp_{V,*,A'}\lambda_w\, B_{A'}\,v_{A'}^*\chi_p=\chi_{p_V}\,Q_VB_A\,\lambda_v.$$
To verify the equality, take adjuncts under $p_{V,A'}^*\dashv Rp_{V,*,A'}$. By the defining exchange counit formula and the defining scalar counit formula, the transpose of the left side is $Q(w_A^*\varepsilon_{p,A,E})$ after the canonical identifications
$$p_{V,A'}^*v_{A'}^*Q_YRp_{*,A}E\cong Q_{p^{-1}(V)}w_A^*p_A^*Rp_{*,A}E.$$
For the right side, substitute $\varepsilon_{p_V,A}p_{V,A}^*B_A=w_A^*\varepsilon_{p,A}$ from the exchange definition; naturality of $\lambda$ gives the same map. The pullback identifications agree by Step 1. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves the square. This is precisely mate pasting, with no assumption that $Q$ preserves $D^+$.

proof.text:
Let $j_V:X_V\hookrightarrow p^{-1}(V)$ and let $e_R:w_R^*j_{!,R}\cong j_{V!,R}v_{X,R}^*$ be the degreewise open base-change isomorphism. The cited open base-change node specifies $e_R^{-1}$ as the open adjunct of the pulled-back open unit. Steps 1 and 3 therefore give
$$j_{V!,A'}\lambda_{v_X}\,e_{A'}\,w_{A'}^*\beta_j=\beta_{j_V}\,Q(e_A)\,\lambda_w.$$
For completeness, invert the open scalar and base-change isomorphisms and take their open adjuncts. Both are the scalar extension of $v_X^*\eta_{j,A}$, followed by the same restriction/scalar identification from Step 1; hence their adjuncts, and then the original maps, agree. On a K-flat representative Step 2 allows the equivalent calculation before sheafification: both maps are $x\otimes a'\mapsto x\otimes a'$ on the unique open summand and zero on the other summands. This proves the equation for arbitrary unbounded inputs, with the precise open-unit normalization.

proof.text:
On the restricted compactification the compact-support exchange is the proper exchange followed by the open exchange:
$$C_{f,v,R}=Rp_{V,*,R}(e_R)\circ B_R(j_{!,R}(-)).$$
This is exactly the normalization in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. Substitute this and $q_f=Rp_{*,A'}\beta_j\circ\chi_p$ into $C_{f,v,A'}v^*q_f$. Naturality of $B_{A'}$ moves $v^*Rp_{*,A'}\beta_j$ through the proper exchange. Apply Step 11 to the adjacent proper coefficient/exchange factors, and Step 12 to the adjacent open coefficient/exchange factors. The result is
$$q_{f_V,v_X^*M}\,Q_V(C_{f,v,A}(M))$$
under $v^*Q_Y\cong Q_Vv^*$ and $v_X^*Q_X\cong Q_{X_V}v_X^*$. This gives the requested open-restriction equation on all of $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$.

Finally insert the coefficient unit $Q_T(A_T[0])\cong A'_T[0]$. On the representatives of Step 1 this is multiplication $a\otimes b'\mapsto\varphi(a)b'$. In Step 3 the open comparison is the same map on the open and zero off it. For proper maps the cited unital projection-mate statement says that projection against the tensor unit is the identity. Thus the projection square at $K=A_Y[0]$ is the unit square, and the counit transposes and open-unit transposes used throughout preserve this identification. Identity proper maps and identity opens give identity scalar maps; the composition and refinement squares already proved consequently preserve the coefficient unit as well. These verifications use neither smooth purity nor exceptional-pullback coefficient comparison.
